sections.h2: What happens to tenants when a Vermont landlord sells a rental?
sections.html:
A sale does not by itself end a tenancy in Vermont, and the landlord still needs a legal reason and a written notice to end it. The state's residential rental law sits in Title 9, Chapter 137, and the rules below come from the statutes and the Vermont Judiciary.

The one provision that speaks to a sale directly is 9 V.S.A. § 4467(d). A landlord who has contracted to sell the building may end a tenancy that has no written rental agreement on at least 30 days of actual notice.

Security deposits move with the property. When the landlord's interest ends, the deposit must be transferred to the new landlord, who must give the tenant actual notice of the new landlord's name and address (9 V.S.A. § 4461(f)).

sections.h2: How much notice does a Vermont landlord have to give?
sections.html:
The notice period depends on the reason and on whether there is a written lease. Section 4467 sets these periods.

SituationNotice
Nonpayment of rent14 days
Breach of a material lease term30 days before the termination date
Criminal, drug or violent activity that threatens other residents14 days
No written agreement, monthly rent, tenant of two years or less60 days
No written agreement, monthly rent, tenant of more than two years90 days
No written agreement, weekly rent21 days
No written agreement, landlord has contracted to sell the building30 days
Written lease, no-cause ending, tenant of two years or less30 days before the end of the stated term
Written lease, no-cause ending, tenant of more than two years60 days before the end of the stated term

The notice must state the termination date. An eviction case must be filed within 60 days of the termination date in the notice, or the notice cannot support a judgment. Accepting rent after termination generally does not waive the landlord's remedies for breach or no-cause termination, and accepting partial rent does not waive remedies for nonpayment.

sections.h2: Can a landlord change the locks or shut off utilities to speed up a sale?
sections.html:
No. The Vermont Judiciary states that a landlord may not remove a tenant without a court order, and may not change the locks, shut off utilities or remove belongings without one, citing 9 V.S.A. § 4463.

A written notice can be delivered by hand, by first-class mail to the tenant's last known address, or by certified mail. Some towns require more notice than the statute, and subsidized rentals such as Section 8 carry extra requirements, so check the lease and any program rules.

sections.h2: What does the Vermont eviction process look like?
sections.html:
An eviction, which Vermont calls ejectment, is filed in the Civil Division of the Superior Court in the county where the property sits. The Judiciary's page describes these steps.

  1. Serve a written termination notice with the grounds and the termination date.
  2. Wait until the date passes, then file within 60 days with the complaint, a copy of the lease if written, the notice, and the CARES Act declaration (form 100-00031).
  3. A sheriff or constable serves the tenant, and the landlord files the return of service.
  4. The tenant generally has 21 days after service to file a written answer. If none is filed, the landlord may seek a default judgment.
  5. A judge decides at hearing or trial whether the tenant can be evicted and whether either side owes money.
  6. If the landlord wins, the court issues a writ of possession, and the tenant has 14 days after service to leave.

A landlord can ask the court to order past-due rent paid into escrow while the case is pending (12 V.S.A. § 4853a). If the tenant misses a payment, the landlord is entitled to immediate possession and the tenant must leave within 7 days. A writ is effective for 60 days after it issues, and the landlord may dispose of remaining belongings on the later of 15 days after the writ is served or the date the landlord legally retakes possession.

The timeline matters to a seller because a buyer who wants vacant possession may wait for a case to run its course. Either side may appeal legal errors to the Vermont Supreme Court.

sections.h2: What are a tenant's rights while the landlord is trying to sell?
sections.html:
A tenant keeps the same protections whether or not the house is listed. They include the implied warranty of habitability, protection from retaliation, and rules on rent increases and deposits.

  • Under 9 V.S.A. § 4457, the landlord is treated as promising premises that are safe, clean and fit for human habitation, and a rental agreement cannot waive this promise. The unit needs heat that can safely provide a reasonable amount of warmth, and adequate water with hot and cold lines.
  • Under § 4465, a landlord may not retaliate against a tenant who complains to a government agency about a health or safety violation, complains to the landlord about a violation, or joins a tenant group. A termination notice within 90 days of a municipal or state violation notice, for reasons other than unpaid rent, is presumed retaliatory.
  • Under § 4455, rent is due without demand, and a rent increase takes effect on the first day of the next rental period after at least 60 days of actual notice.
  • Under § 4456, a tenant must not damage the premises or interfere with other tenants' peaceful enjoyment, and can end a tenancy by giving actual notice at least one rental payment period before the termination date unless the lease says otherwise.

A landlord who files a notice to sell soon after a code complaint should expect the retaliation presumption to come up.

sections.h2: What are the Vermont security deposit rules?
sections.html:
A landlord must return the deposit with a written itemized statement within 14 days after learning the tenant has moved out or abandoned the unit, or after the move-out date if the tenant gave notice. Seasonal rentals that are not a primary residence get 60 days.

A landlord may keep money only for unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear and tear, unpaid utility or other charges owed, and removal of abandoned articles. If the landlord misses the 14 days, the right to withhold any part is lost, and a willful failure makes the landlord liable for double the amount wrongfully withheld plus attorney's fees and costs. A tenant who is owed a deposit can use small claims court for up to $10,000, and Brattleboro and Burlington have additional deposit rules.

For a seller, an accurate deposit ledger is part of the closing package, because the buyer takes over the duty to return each deposit.

sections.h2: Who inspects Vermont rentals, and what does that mean before a sale?
sections.html:
The Division of Fire Safety, within the Department of Public Safety, is the primary enforcer of the Rental Housing Health and Safety Code under Act 181, signed June 7, 2022, and the program took effect January 1, 2024. Local health officials keep concurrent authority and can still inspect.

The program is complaint-based. Tenants first contact the owner or manager, and if that fails they can submit an online complaint form that routes to the regional office for the property's ZIP code. The Division has regional offices in Williston, Waterbury, Rutland and Springfield. Short-term rentals count as rentals, but the Division inspects them only in response to complaints.

sections.h2: What tax and reporting items does a landlord face when selling a Vermont rental?
sections.html:
Landlords who rent residential property for 30 or more days in a row file a Landlord Certificate (Form LRC-140) with the Department of Taxes each year for each property with a rented unit. A landlord who does not file may be fined, with interest.

On the sale itself, the Department of Taxes lists the property transfer tax at 1.25 percent for a year-round home that is a long-term rental, and 3.40 percent for a non-principal residence fit for year-round habitation that is not a long-term rental. Add the 0.22 percent Clean Water Surcharge in both cases, and ask your attorney which category your building falls into. Vermont also treats a landlord's certificate carefully: under 32 V.S.A. § 9602 the Commissioner may assess the higher rate if a landlord certificate is filed without a real landlord-tenant relationship.

A nonresident landlord should expect 2.5 percent withholding on the sale price, filed by the buyer on Form RW-171 within 30 days, unless a Commissioner's Certificate is obtained.

sections.h2: Where can landlords and tenants get help in Vermont?
sections.html:
The Judiciary lists three starting points: the Access and Resource Center at 802-879-1185 or selfhelp@vtcourts.gov, the CVOEO tenant hotline at 802-864-0099, and Vermont Legal Aid at 800-889-2047.

Vermont has 14 counties, and a case is filed in the county where the rental sits. Chittenden County, which includes Burlington, had 168,323 residents in the 2020 Census and is the most populous. Median gross rent statewide was $1,234 for 2020 to 2024, and the median value of owner-occupied homes was $316,600, according to the Census Bureau.

faqs.q: Can a Vermont landlord end a tenancy because the house is being sold?
faqs.a: Only with proper notice. If there is no written agreement and the landlord has contracted to sell the building, 9 V.S.A. § 4467(d) allows at least 30 days of actual notice.

faqs.q: How many days does a landlord have to return a security deposit in Vermont?
faqs.a: 14 days after learning the tenant moved out, or after the move-out date if notice was given, with an itemized written statement. Seasonal rentals get 60 days.

faqs.q: How much notice is needed for nonpayment of rent?
faqs.a: 14 days under 9 V.S.A. § 4467(a). A written lease does not lengthen it.

faqs.q: Does the deposit transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: Yes. Under § 4461(f), the deposit transfers to the new landlord, who must give the tenant actual notice of the name and address.

faqs.q: Can a Vermont landlord remove a tenant without going to court?
faqs.a: No. The Judiciary says a landlord may not remove a tenant, change locks, shut off utilities or remove belongings without a court order.

faqs.q: How long does a tenant have to leave after a writ of possession?
faqs.a: 14 days after service of the writ, or 7 days after a missed rent escrow payment.
